reference_sql:
SELECT pr.promo_type, COUNT(DISTINCT pr.promo_id) AS n_promotions, COUNT(*) AS n_listings
FROM promotions pr
JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.promo_id = pr.promo_id
GROUP BY pr.promo_type
alternatives: WITH promo_sizes AS (SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products FROM promotion_products GROUP BY promo_id) SELECT pr.promo_type, COUNT(*) AS n_promotions, SUM(s.n_products) AS n_listings FROM promotions pr JOIN promo_sizes s ON s.promo_id = pr.promo_id GROUP BY pr.promo_type
SELECT pr.promo_type, COUNT(DISTINCT pp.promo_id) AS n_promotions, COUNT(pp.product_id) AS n_listings FROM promotion_products pp JOIN promotions pr ON pr.promo_id = pp.promo_id GROUP BY 1

other_way.sql: WITH promo_sizes AS (SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products FROM promotion_products GROUP BY promo_id) SELECT pr.promo_type, COUNT(*) AS n_promotions, SUM(s.n_products) AS n_listings FROM promotions pr JOIN promo_sizes s ON s.promo_id = pr.promo_id GROUP BY pr.promo_type
other_way.tradeoff: Counting each promotion's products in a step first keeps one row per promotion, but COUNT(DISTINCT) does it in one query.
